The lane gets b88 (its east end); the sky gets the mist (b86, sky × Scale/World); the plaza's gap is diagnosed, not built — c127 asks for a presence count first, because the east half's supply has been re-tuned four times and a fifth blind tune is how a domain gets a polish streak. rationale: RUNG 4, both halves, because smallDiff fires and the ladder says a firing signal is a spent rung — the last batch's cart and sundial were structural and still the batch's median was polish-sized. Thirty seconds at the wide shot, seed 42, early-summer noon: the river runs the full height of the frame through its centre and is a flat blue slab with faint streaks — one rowboat sometimes, two swans; the far-bank lawn and the plaza are empty at noon; the sky is plain blue with three clouds and has never been anything but clear, raining or snowing. So b85 THE BET (4b, river × Scale/World, 75 min, a 150–300-line diff invited): an EYOT — an island in the river's east half with a willow, a shingle bank and reeds, the boat's channel kept clear on the west, the swans given a third bank, ducks nesting on it in spring; WATER cells become a new tile, speciesKinds and tileKinds move and the baseline is re-pinned. b86 (4a, sky × Scale/World, 60 min, high): RIVER MIST — a rate-capped mistF() that rises off the water on still, clear mornings after a wet or cold night, thickest over the river and the low east ground at sunUp, gone by mid-morning; the backdrop's HAZE is already a consumer (drawRoofRow mixes 0.55 into it) and the morning tap (sunUp + 0.5) lands a visitor inside it. b87 c125: the concert audience walks round the bandstand to the deck (life × Connect, medium) — 290 of 418 far-side evening retirements were the audience, and #85 showed the deck's evening needs people already on the far side. b88 c122: the lane's east end becomes a real end (lane × Connect, medium-low) — nothing has ever left or arrived by x 138 in 86 iterations. b89 c123: weathercocks and lookAt names them (roofs × Polish, low). Order: bet first, mist second, so both are built while the plan is fresh.

queue.brief: c122 — the lane 12 iterations back, its longest gap. In 86 iterations nothing has ever arrived or left by the lane's EAST end (x 138, past PARK_GATE): spawnLaneAgent enters at x −2.5 only, every exit goes west or up an alley, the cart goes west or back north. Make the east end a real end: a share of lane arrivals (measured at the choice) enter from the east and walk WEST along the lane, and lane leavers whose last stop is east of the cross street (x > ~64) leave by the east end instead of walking the whole lane back — a routeToExit() that picks the nearer end. On market days a share of the cart's departures could go east too. The observable outcome is two-way traffic on the lane bridge and people appearing from behind the far-bank gatehouse.
